texts.preamble: Fable Food Products Pvt. Ltd. vs State Of Gujarat on 4 February, 2020 Author: A.Y. Kogje Bench: A.Y. Kogje C/Sca/18506/2017 Order
texts.facts: This group of petitions under Article 226 of the Constitution of India are filed for setting aside the order in Appeal made by the Food and Safety Appellate Tribunal, in the respective Appeals under the provisions of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006. Considering the similarity of the issues involved and the submissions made, all the three petitions are being taken up for joint hearing and disposal with the consent of the parties. 2. The facts are narrated from Special Civil Application No.18506/2017. The petitioner has challenged the order of the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal, Gandhinagar dated 17.06.2017 in Appeal No.76/2015 and the order dated 09.07.2014 in Adjudication Application No.12/2014 passed by the Adjudicating Officer and Additional Resident Collector, Vadodara. By the impugned order, the order of the Additional Collector imposing fine of Rs.25,000/- each on the petitioners has been confirmed. Fable Food Products Pvt. Ltd. vs State Of Gujarat on 4 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126503982/ 1 3. It is the case of the petitioners that the petitioners are holding a License and are engaged in the business of manufacturing of food products and milk products like 'ghee'. During a surprise visit on 09.04.2012 at a Store in Vadodara, a sample of 'Shradhdha Gaynu Ghee' was sent for laboratory analysis and was found to be sub-standard. It is in this regard, the proceedings were undertaken and sanction for complaint was granted. After the procedure, a fine of Rs.25,000/- each was imposed.
texts.arguments: 4. Learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that the proceedings initiated are vitiated on account of non-granting of sufficient opportunity of hearing and non-supply of complete set of documents. 5. It is submitted that sample of ghee was taken on 09.04.2012 and the report was not received within a period of 14 days, thereby depriving the petitioner of the valuable right to get the same re-tested. It is also submitted that the proceedings are vitiated as the case was not filed within a period of one year of taking of the sample. 6. As against this, learned Assistant Government Pleader has opposed the petition contending that the authorities have given concurrent finding of facts and there is conclusive evidence of the milk product 'ghee' being sub-standard and hence, imposing of fine was justified. The technical objection raised by the petitioners are non-significant and has not caused any breach to the petitioners right. 7. "(8) Ld. Advocate Shri N.S. Wafi has stated in his written arguments that the provisions of Food Safety and Standard Rules-3(1)(6) read with Section-68(4) of the Food Safety and Standard (2006) act has been violated. Further, Learned Advocate Shri N.S. Wafi has stated vide his written arguments that one fourth part of the sample has not been given by the complainant officer to the government accredited laboratory. Further, the Ld. Advocate for the applicants has also presented some judgments alongwith this appeal.
